claim: FS2: a 1.75 m fabric screen gives privacy from standing people
law: ANSUR II standing eye height 1,421 to 1,753 mm
check: The fabric top at about 1,550 mm hides the patient from most standing adults, and also hides the patient from staff except at the foot end

claim: FS2: the post-and-rail screen stands a 178 N push
law: One side frame (a third of the screen mass) about a cross-foot tip 124 mm out, push at 1,372 mm; with and without 10 kg of bags on its feet
check: About 3.5 N bare and 12.4 N with 10 kg of ballast (independent review 2026-11-12: weak, ballast added for a fair comparison): it tips at a touch, like FS1's free ends

claim: FS2: FR fabric meets NFPA 701 and can be wiped
law: Medline 3-panel FR vinyl screen 'meets the standard UL 94' (Staples listing); Still Water privacy panels 'pass the NFPA 701' (Direct Textile Store)
check: UL 94 is a plastics test, not a curtain test, so it is no evidence toward NFPA 701 (independent review 2026-11-12: weak); coated fabric with an NFPA 701 report exists; the lot's report is to source

claim: FS2: costs about the USD 120 target
law: Medline FR vinyl 3-panel screen USD 210.79 (Staples); Winco 3130 3-panel screen USD 235.57 (MDMaxx); two screens needed for a U
check: About USD 422 for two of the cheaper screens at retail; a made FS2 frame of aluminium tube and FR fabric would cost less, to assess, so this compares retail with FS1's parts cost (independent review 2026-11-12: weak)

claim: FS2: one person carries and sets it
law: Model mass with FR coated fabric at 0.45 kg/m2 (A12)
check: 11.9 kg; 7 posts, 12 rails and 6 screens to assemble

claim: FS3: the cot carries a patient's pull on the screen frame
law: MSF field hospital bed maximum load 120 kg; frame clamped to both side rails with four M6 clamps
check: The pull goes into the cot, which the patient is lying on, so the frame cannot tip on its own; clamp slip on a round rail and the cot's own tipping when a patient pulls sideways at 1.2 m are to assess

claim: FS3: gives privacy and a contact boundary at the head and upper body
law: Screen from the cot rail to 1200 mm, 700 mm along each side from the head
check: Covers the head and chest of a lying patient; legs and the rest of the cot are open. Same sightlines as FS1 for the covered part

claim: FS3: staff can clear the head for resuscitation
law: Four rail clamps with M6 bolts as drawn
check: Unbolting four clamps takes a minute or more; a lift-off frame on sockets would be needed to clear it in seconds (to design if FS3 is chosen)

law: FR coated fabric at the patient's head, about 1.4 m2
check: Much less fire load than FS1 (fabric about 0.6 kg against 4 kg of PP sheet), but fabric hangs within 0.1 m of the pillow; an FR report is needed

law: US 11,369,208 B2 (active): canopy of U-shaped frames hinged to a bed with a top wall; US 12,213,925 B2 (active): screen clamped to bed side rails
check: FS3 has no top wall and no rail-clamp bracket with a slider knob as claimed, but sits close to both: an FTO opinion is needed (FXS-FTO-001)

claim: FS1 at P18 with a frosted upper band (the team's semi-transparent upper panels)
law: Same plan with P18 duos (FXP-PLT-001 module); free-end leaf at 1.8 m (FXP-PLT-001 P2)
check: Panels 6.05 kg from 4 sheets against 4.03 kg from 2; the free-end leaf fails cold (FXP-PLT-001 P2: flat h_cr 1,441 mm < 1,800 mm); a frosted FR film or mesh band needs its own fire report and staff still see only shapes through it
